source.fragmentationNote: KTU 1.3 + 1.4 are the best-preserved tablets of the Baal Cycle. KTU 1.3: 6 columns, approximately 245 preserved lines with scattered lacunae (heavier damage at col i bottom and col vi). KTU 1.4: 8 columns, approximately 410 preserved lines — the most substantial single tablet of the Cycle and source of the major palace-building, window-debate, and theophany passages. Lacunae marked per project lacuna-bracket convention: [...] = total lacuna; [text] = restored from parallels; <text> = editorial addition; {text} = editorial deletion.
source.scriptNote: Ugaritic alphabetic cuneiform — 30 letters + word divider, 1:1 transliteration-to-Unicode mapping. Strict KTU transliteration: every alef explicitly marked as ʾa/ʾi/ʾu. Cuneiform output in this file was produced mechanically by the project's translit_to_ugaritic.py helper from each line's transliteration — not hand-authored. The ' . ' word-separator in standard KTU transliteration is converted to the Ugaritic word divider 𐎟 (U+1039F) between cuneiform tokens.

i18n.en: [KTU 1.3 col i opens after the resolution of the Yammu conflict. The column's first lines are damaged; preserved text shows a banquet at Baʿlu's residence with the cup-bearer attending him. The famous 'mighty Baʿlu' banquet-scene introduces the palace-building arc.]

lines.notes: '…the desire of gold(?).' mḥmd 'desire, precious thing' (cf. Hebrew maḥmād Lam 2:4); ḫrṣ 'gold' — banquet luxury-vocabulary.
'He set [out] wine drawn-by-hand into the cup.' yšt = G-yqtl of šty 'set / pour'; ḥsp 'drawn off, ladled' (cf. Hebrew ḥāśap); ks 'cup' — the cup-bearer's act.
'…into the krpn-bowl, blood (= wine) of trees.' krpn = large drinking-vessel; dm ʿṣm 'blood of trees' = wine, the standard kenning (cf. Deut 32:14 dam ʿēnāb 'blood of the grape').
'He arose, he prepared (table) and served him food.' qm 'arise'; yṯʿr 'he arranges, prepares' (D-yqtl); yšlḥmnh 'he feeds him' (Š-yqtl of lḥm 'to eat'). The cup-bearer's serving sequence.
'He cut a (slice of) breast before him.' ybrd 'he carves' (G-yqtl of brd); ṯd 'breast, joint' (cf. Hebrew šād 'breast'); l pnwh 'before him.' Banquet meat-portion.
'With a knife salted, a portion of fatling.' ḥrb mlḥt 'salted knife' = ritual carving-blade; mrʾi 'fatling, fattened animal' (cf. Hebrew mĕrîʾ; cf. Amos 5:22). The cultic-feast vocabulary.

'He stood, he served (drink) and gave him drink.' ndd 'stood, took post'; yʿšr 'he made (the table) abundant' (D-yqtl of ʿšr); yšqynh 'he gave him to drink' (Š-yqtl of šqy). Cf. Hebrew šāqâ 'give drink' (Gen 24:18).
'He placed a cup in his hand.' bd-h = 'in his hand' (b + yd + 3ms suffix; with assimilation bd). Standard cup-handling formula.
'A krpn-bowl in both his hands.' klʾat ydh 'his two hands' — dual-handed grasping of a great cup; characteristic of divine drinking scenes.
'A great vessel mighty, RʾIDN(?).' bk rb 'a great vessel'; ʿẓm 'mighty, massive'; rʾidn uncertain — possibly a vessel-type name.
'…a vessel of the heavens, a holy cup.' mt here a measure-vessel; šmm 'heavens'; ks qdš 'holy cup' — the sanctified drinking-vessel.

'…no woman shall behold it.' l tphnh 'she shall not see it' (G-yqtl 3fs negative + 3ms suffix; cf. Hebrew pānâ); ʾaṯt 'woman, wife.' The famous gender-restricted cup-line (Smith & Pitard 2009 Vol 2 pp. 100-104).
'…the krpn-bowl ʾAṯiratu shall not see.' Even ʾAṯiratu (the mother of the gods) is excluded from beholding the holy cup. Cf. Smith-Pitard 2009 vol 2 on the all-male divine banquet.
'A thousand jars he takes in (his) mixture.' ʾalp kd 'a thousand jars (of wine)'; ḫmr 'wine, fermented mixture' (cf. Hebrew ḥemer).
'Ten thousand he mixes in his mixing.' rbt 'ten thousand'; ymsk = G-yqtl of msk 'to mix' (cf. Hebrew māsak; Isa 19:14). The thousand // ten-thousand pair-formula in banquet context.
'He arose, he sang and chanted.' ybd = D-yqtl of bdy 'to sing, intone'; yšr = G-yqtl of šyr (cf. Hebrew šîr 'to sing'). The post-meal song-performance.

'…cymbals in the hand of the Sweet One.' mṣltm 'cymbals' (cf. Hebrew mĕṣiltayim 1 Chr 13:8 — pair-form 'two cymbals'); nʿm 'pleasant/sweet one' — a divine epithet, possibly of the singer-deity. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: the cymbal-pair is part of the same musical lexicon as Ps 150.
'…the hero, sweet of voice, sang.' ġzr 'hero, warrior'; ṭb ql 'good of voice, sweet-voiced.' The hero-as-singer image.

'…before Baʿlu on the heights of Ṣapunu.' ʿl bʿl 'before Baʿlu'; ṣrrt ṣpn 'heights / peaks of Ṣapunu' (Baʿlu's mountain-abode, modern Jebel al-Aqraʿ; cf. Ps 48:3 yarkĕtê ṣāpôn 'recesses of the north').
'Baʿlu beheld his daughters.' ytmr 'he sees, beholds' (Gt-yqtl of mr/ʾmr; or a denominative); bnt 'daughters' — Baʿlu's three daughters Pidray, Ṭallay, Arṣay (introduced below).
'He saw Pidrayu daughter of light.' pdry 'Pidray' (the first daughter); bt ʾar 'daughter of light/luminous-one' = her epithet. Cf. KTU 1.3 III 7.

'Then Ṭallayu daughter of showers.' ʾapn 'then, indeed'; ṭly 'Ṭallay' (the second daughter — 'Dewy-One,' from ṭl 'dew'); bt rb 'daughter of the abundant-rain / showers' (cf. Hebrew rĕbîbîm 'showers' Ps 65:11).
'…the hand of Pidru, the hand of…' Severely fragmentary; pdr is a related deity-name.
'…clouds(?).' ʿrpt 'clouds' (cf. Hebrew ʿărāpel 'thick cloud'); Baʿlu's storm-attribute.

i18n.en: [KTU 1.3 col ii: the column opens with ʿAnatu, the warrior consort-goddess, beginning her cosmic battle. The lines that follow contain the most explicit female-warrior-deity passage in the entire Northwest-Semitic corpus (Smith & Pitard 2009 vol 2 pp. 138-176; Day 2000 pp. 132-150). MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE — the warrior-goddess imagery and the wading-through-blood motif have generated extensive comparative scholarship.]

lines.notes: 'ʿAnatu shuts(?) the gate of P[idr]…' tġr 'she shuts, secures' (G-yqtl 3fs of ġr; cf. Hebrew sāgar). The battle-preparation.
'She does battle in the valley.' tmtḫṣ = Gt-yqtl 3fs of mḫṣ 'to smite' (the same root as Yammu's defeat); b ʿmq 'in the valley' (cf. Hebrew ʿēmeq Josh 7:24). The cosmic-valley as battlefield.
'She contends between two cities.' tḫtṣb = Gt-yqtl 3fs of ḫṣb (cf. Akk. ḫaṣābu; Hebrew ḥṣb 'to hew, contend'); bn qrytm 'between two towns.' Urban-warfare imagery.
'She smites the people of the seashore.' lʾim 'peoples, multitudes'; ḫp ym 'shore of the sea' (cf. Hebrew ḥôp yām Gen 49:13). The coastal massacre.

'She annihilates the humans of the rising of the sun.' tṣmt 'she destroys' (G-yqtl 3fs of ṣmt; cf. Hebrew ṣmt Lev 25:23); ʾadm 'humans, mortals' (cf. Hebrew ʾādām); ṣʾat špš 'going-out / rising of the sun' = east. The east-to-west sweep.
'Beneath her like balls (are) heads.' tḥt h 'beneath her'; kdrt 'balls, spheres' (cf. Akk. kudurru); ryš 'heads' (cf. Hebrew rōʾš). The heads-as-bowling-balls image — a signature ʿAnat-battle motif.
'Above her like locusts (are) hands.' ʿlh 'above her'; ʾirbym 'locusts' (cf. Hebrew ʾarbeh Joel 1:4); kp 'hands, palms.' Dismembered hands swarming like locusts in flight.

'Like reapers (heaping) sheaves, (are) the hands of soldiers.' qṣm 'reapers' (cf. Hebrew qōṣĕrîm); ġrmn 'heaps of grain, sheaves' (cf. Hebrew gārmâ); mhr 'soldier, warrior.' The harvest-as-battle simile.

'She ties heads to her back.' ʿtkt 'she binds, ties' (G-pf 3fs of ʿtk); rʾišt 'heads' (pl); bmt 'back, high-place' (cf. Hebrew bāmâ — both 'back' and 'high-place'). ʿAnatu wears severed heads as a trophy-belt.
'She fastens hands at her belt.' šnst 'she binds tight' (Š-pf 3fs); kpt 'hands' (pl of kp); ḥbš 'belt, girdle' (cf. Hebrew ḥĕbeš).

**THE FAMOUS LINE — ʿAnat wades**: 'She plunges (knee-deep) into the blood of warriors.' tġll = G-yqtl 3fs of ġll 'to immerse, sink into' (cf. Hebrew gll); dm 'blood'; ḏmr 'warriors, soldiers' (cf. Hebrew zĕmîrôt 'songs' but here zmr = 'guard, warrior,' cf. Exod 15:2 ʿozzî wĕzimrāt yāh). Most explicit female-warrior-deity passage in NWS corpus (Smith-Pitard 2009 vol 2 pp. 161-164). LENS-RISK SITE.

**THE FAMOUS LINE (continued)**: 'Up to the throat in the gore of soldiers.' ḫlqm 'up to the neck/throat' (cf. Akk. ḫalqu; Hebrew ḥōq 'neck'); mmʿ 'gore, entrails' (cf. Hebrew mēʿîm 'entrails' Gen 25:23). The wading-through-blood image. Cf. Isa 63:1-6 for the closest Hebrew Bible parallel (Yahweh's bloody robes in Edom).

'Until she is sated, she does battle in (her) house.' ʿd tšbʿ 'until she is satisfied' (cf. Hebrew śābaʿ 'be sated'); tmtḫṣ 'she battles' (Gt-yqtl 3fs); b bt 'in the house' — the battle moves into ʿAnatu's hall.
'She contends between two tables.' bn ṯlḥnm 'between two tables' (cf. Hebrew šulḥān). The transition from external battle to the indoor banquet-as-battle.
'(The blood of) soldier(s) is wiped from the tables(?).' ymḫ 'is wiped clean' (G-yqtl 3ms passive of mḥy; cf. Hebrew māḥâ 'to wipe out'). Domestic-battle clean-up.

'The thrones are overturned to (= become) soldiers.' yhpk 'is overturned' (G-yqtl 3ms of hpk; cf. Hebrew hāpak Gen 19:25); ksʾat 'thrones, seats.' The furniture-as-warriors image — the room itself fights.
'Footstools (are turned) to thrones, the throne-rooms to halls(?).' ṯpṯ 'footstool, judgment-seat'; hdm 'footstool' (cf. Hebrew hădōm Ps 110:1); hkl 'temple, palace' (cf. Hebrew hêkāl).
'Greatly she battles, and she beholds…'. mʾid 'very, greatly' (cf. Hebrew mĕʾōd); tmtḫṣn 'she battles' (Gt-yqtl 3fs with n-ending).
'She contends, and ʿAnat exults.' tḥdy 'she rejoices' (G-yqtl 3fs of ḥdy; cf. Hebrew ḥādâ 'to rejoice'). The post-battle exultation.

'Her liver(/heart) swells with laughter.' tġdd 'it swells, expands' (G-yqtl 3fs of gdd; cf. Hebrew gādal); kbdh 'her liver' = her inward seat of emotion (cf. Hebrew kābēd as emotive-organ Prov 7:23); ṣḥq 'laughter' (cf. Hebrew ṣĕḥōq Gen 21:6). The visceral-joy formula.

'Her heart is filled with gladness.' ymlʾu 'it is filled' (G-yqtl 3ms passive of mlʾ); lb 'heart' (cf. Hebrew lēb); šmḫt 'gladness, joy' (cf. Hebrew śimḥâ). The internal-rejoicing formula — the post-battle exuberance.
'The liver of ʿAnatu (is in) triumph.' tšyt 'success, triumph' (cf. Hebrew tûšiyyâ Prov 8:14).
'She plunges her hands in dust(?).' tġl  uncertain; bdm 'hands'; ʿpr 'dust' — ritual cleansing/marking-with-dust after the slaughter.
'She places (her) tooth(?) in the dust.' Cleansing-after-battle imagery; the body returning to a state of peace.
'A thousand of gold, seven of … sons(?).' Numerical pair, lost context.
'She uncovers, she washes her hand.' tgly 'she uncovers, reveals' (G-yqtl 3fs of gly); trḥṣ 'she washes' (G-yqtl 3fs of rḥṣ; cf. Hebrew rāḥaṣ). The ritual-cleansing post-battle.
'…the Maiden ʿAnatu, her fingers…' btlt ʿnt 'Maiden ʿAnatu' = ʿAnatu's standard epithet (cf. Hebrew bĕtûlâ 'maiden'); ʾuṣbʿt 'fingers' (cf. Hebrew ʾeṣbaʿ).

'…the Sister-in-law of nations.' ybmt lʾimm 'sister-in-law / progenitress of peoples' = ʿAnatu's epithet (cf. Hebrew yĕbāmâ Deut 25:7-10; in Ugaritic context 'kinswoman of the peoples'). Translation contested.
'The Maiden ʿAnatu washes her hand…' Repetition of the washing-formula.
'…[her finger]s, (she) the Sister-in-law of nations.' Parallelism with line 30.

'[She washes her hand] in the blood of warriors.' The blood here is BOTH the substance of her battle AND her washing-water — the paradoxical purification-by-blood (cf. Smith-Pitard 2009 vol 2 pp. 168-170).
'[Her fingers in the gore of] soldiers.' Restored parallel.
'…thrones to soldiers.' Likely a return-formula or transition.
'…tables to armies.' ṯlḥnt 'tables' (pl); ṣbʾim 'armies, hosts' (cf. Hebrew ṣĕbāʾôt 'hosts').
'…footstools to soldiers.' The furniture-as-army-imagery continues.
'She draws water and washes.' tḥsp 'she ladles, draws' (G-yqtl 3fs of ḥsp; cf. Hebrew ḥāśap 'lay bare, draw out'); mh 'water' (cf. Hebrew mayim).

'…dew of heaven, oil of earth.' ṭl 'dew' (cf. Hebrew ṭal Gen 27:28); šmn 'oil, fat' (cf. Hebrew šemen). The cosmic-cleansing formula — heaven's dew and earth's oil as the post-battle ablution. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. Gen 27:28 ṭal haššāmayim ūmišmannê hāʾāreṣ.

'…showers of the Cloud-Rider.' rbb 'showers, droplets' (cf. Hebrew rĕbîbîm Ps 65:11); rkb ʿrpt 'Rider of the Clouds' = Baʿlu's signature epithet — STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. Ps 68:5 rōkēb bāʿărābôt 'rider on the clouds' (= Yahweh).
'Dew of heaven pours upon her.' tskh 'pours over her' (G-yqtl 3fs of nsk; cf. Hebrew nāsak 'to pour libation').
'…showers pour upon her (from) the stars.' kbkbm 'stars' (cf. Hebrew kôkābîm). The astral-shower formula.
'[She adorns herself with] purple-dye(?), a thousand acres.' ʾanḫb 'purple-shell-dye, murex-purple' (cf. Akk. anḫabu); šd 'field, acre.' Cosmetic-adornment after battle.
'[Gol]d-(stringed)(?) she took her [l]yre.' kinnārum 'lyre' (cf. Hebrew kinnôr Gen 4:21; the same root). ʿAnatu turns to music after battle — the post-violence cultural-marker.

i18n.en: [KTU 1.3 col iii: top mostly preserved. The post-battle ʿAnat is approached by Baʿlu's two messengers Gpn-wa-Ugar ('Vine-and-Field') with the famous 'word of tree, whisper of stone' revelation-formula. The same overlay-formula recurs from KTU 1.1 iii — the cosmic-speech mystery.]

lines.notes: '…she destroyed his calf.' tsmt 'she annihilated' (G-pf 3fs of ṣmt); ʿgl 'calf' (cf. Hebrew ʿēgel Exod 32). Possibly reference to ʿAnatu's prior killing of a divine-calf figure.
'She set teeth(?), gift(?)…' Fragmentary; possibly a list of post-battle trophies.
'…of Dimaron(?).' dmrn possibly a divine name or epithet — sometimes read as a Baʿlu-title.
'ʿAṯtaru answered…' ʿṯtr 'ʿAṯtaru' (the morning-star deity); the divine-assembly responding.
'She contends, she takes her bow.' qšt 'bow' (cf. Hebrew qešet); tʾiḫd 'she seizes' (G-yqtl 3fs of ʾḫd; cf. Hebrew ʾāḥaz).
'…tree of the city(?).' ʿṣ 'tree, wood'; qrt 'town' (cf. Hebrew qiryâ). Lost context.
'Baʿlu sees the going of his sister.' hlk 'going, walking'; ʾaḫth 'his sister' = ʿAnatu (Baʿlu's sister-consort). Baʿlu observes ʿAnatu's approach from afar.
'The progress of his father's daughter (he sees).' tdrq 'her stride, advance' (cf. Hebrew derek); ybnt ʾabh 'the daughter of his father' — a kinship formula naming ʿAnatu as Baʿlu's paternal sister.
'He sends out(?) … she destroys.' Fragmentary; possibly relating to Baʿlu's command-message to ʿAnatu.
'…she sends(?) cups(?).' ksm 'cups' (pl of ks); a banquet-vocabulary fragment.
'…he stretches out among the trees, ʿRN(?).' ydy 'he stretches/spreads' (G-yqtl); ʿṣm 'trees.'
'…she carries(?), he places jar of wine.' ḥmr yn 'wine-jar' (cf. Hebrew ḥōmer + yayin).
'…until she is sated he places.' ʿd tšbʿ 'until she is full' — banquet-completion formula.
'…drinking, … fatling-pieces, breast(?).' šty 'drinking'; mrġṯ 'choice cut(?)'; ṯd 'breast' — feast-portions.
'…with a salted knife, a portion of fatling.' Recurring feast-formula (cf. 1.3 i 7).
'…they place wine in a cup of gold.' yn 'wine'; ks ḫrṣ 'cup of gold' — the divine-banquet vessel.
'…blood of trees (wine) in a cup of gold.' Parallel to line 16. The kenning dm ʿṣm = 'wine.'
'…the deeps, the wing of eagles.' tḥmt 'deeps' (cf. Hebrew tĕhôm Gen 1:2); knp nšrm 'wing(s) of eagles' (cf. Hebrew kanpê nešer Exod 19:4). The cosmic-flight imagery.
'…Baʿlu sits like the dwelling of the mountain.' k tbt ġr 'like the seat of the mountain'; Baʿlu enthroned on Ṣapunu.
'…Dagan(?) like the [ea]rth.' dgn 'Dagan' (a grain-deity; Baʿlu's father in some traditions: bn dgn 'son of Dagan').
**THE WORD-OF-TREE FORMULA OPENING**: 'A word for the Maiden ʿAnatu.' rgm 'word, message'; introduces the revelation-formula. Recurring throughout the Cycle (cf. KTU 1.1 iii 12-15; 1.3 IV 13-16).
'Repeat to the Sister-in-law of nations.' ṯny 'repeat, declare again' (D-impv); the messenger-instruction.
'Message of Mighty Baʿlu.' tḥm 'message, oracle'; ʾalʾiyn bʿl 'Mightiest Baʿlu' — standard epithet (note the alef-i in ʾalʾiyn).
'Word of the Mighty One of warriors.' ʾalʾiy qrdm 'Mighty One of heroes' = Baʿlu's epithet; qrd 'warrior' (cf. Akk. qarrādu).
**THE PEACE-FORMULA**: 'Place war in the earth!' qryy 'to set, place' (G-impv); b ʾarṣ 'in the earth'; mlḥmt 'war, battle' (cf. Hebrew milḥāmâ). Cf. Isa 2:4. The repeated 'lay-down-war' oracle.
'Set in the dust love-tokens(?).' ddym 'mandrakes, love-tokens, mounds' (cf. Hebrew dûdāʾîm Gen 30:14); the peace-establishment formula. Cf. KTU 1.1 ii 20.

**THE PEACE-FORMULA (continued)**: 'Pour peace into the midst of the earth!' sk 'pour' (G-impv); šlm 'peace, well-being' (cf. Hebrew šālôm); kbd ʾarṣ 'midst of the earth' (literally 'liver,' inward part).
'…(pour) tranquility into the midst of the fields.' ʾarbdd 'tranquility, calm' (etymology debated; possibly cognate to Akk. rbṣ 'to lie down at rest'); šdm 'fields' (pl of šd).

**THE REVELATION-FORMULA OPENING**: 'There is (a thing) for me, and I will tell you.' ʾiṯ 'there is' (existential particle; cf. Hebrew yēš); ʾargmk 'I will declare to you' (D-yqtl + 2ms suffix). The standard pre-revelation formula.
'A word, and I will repeat it to you.' ʾaṯnyk 'I will repeat to you' (Dt-yqtl + 2ms suffix of ṯny 'repeat').

**THE FAMOUS WORD-OF-TREE-AND-WHISPER-OF-STONE FORMULA**: 'A word of tree and a whisper of stone.' rgm ʿṣ 'speech of wood/tree'; lḫšt 'whisper, secret-speech' (cf. Hebrew lāḥaš 'to whisper, charm'); ʾabn 'stone' (cf. Hebrew ʾeben). The signature mystery-revelation formula; STRONG cross-corpus reach (cf. Hab 2:11 'the stone will cry out from the wall'). Same formula at KTU 1.1 iii 13.
'The converse of heaven with earth.' tʾant 'converse, communication' (cf. ʿnh 'to answer'); the celestial-terrestrial dialogue. Cf. KTU 1.1 iii 14.
'…of the deeps with the stars.' thmt 'deeps' (cf. Hebrew tĕhôm); kbkbm 'stars.' The vertical cosmos-speech: heaven–earth–deep–stars all in conversation. Cf. Ps 19:1-4.

lines.translit: ʾabn . brq . d l . tdʿ . šmm
lines.notes: **THE LIGHTNING-MYSTERY**: 'A stone of lightning that the heavens do not know.' brq 'lightning' (cf. Hebrew bārāq); d l tdʿ 'that does not know' — the hidden-knowledge formula. Baʿlu's lightning as cosmic-secret.
'…a word that humans do not know.' nšm 'humans, mortals' (cf. Hebrew ʾănāšîm). Cf. KTU 1.1 iii 15.
'…and the multitudes of earth do not understand.' tbn = G-yqtl of byn 'to understand' (cf. Hebrew bîn); hmlt ʾarṣ 'multitudes of earth.'
'(But) you and I — I will reveal it.' ʾatm here possibly enclitic (2sg pronominal); ʾibġy 'I will seek out, reveal' (G-yqtl of bġy). The intimate-revelation pact between Baʿlu and ʿAnatu.
'In the midst of my mountain, divine Ṣapunu.' ġry 'my mountain'; ʾil ṣpn 'divine Ṣapunu' = Baʿlu's holy peak.

'In the holy place, on the mountain of my inheritance.' qdš 'holiness, sanctuary' (cf. Hebrew qōdeš); nḥlty 'my inheritance' (cf. Hebrew naḥălâ Exod 15:17). The sanctuary-of-inheritance formula. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. Exod 15:17 'mountain of your inheritance.'
'In the pleasant (place), on the hill of victory.' nʿm 'pleasant, beautiful'; gbʿ 'hill' (cf. Hebrew gibʿâ); tlʾiyt 'triumph, victory' (cf. lʾy 'to prevail').
'ʿAnatu — and she lifted her voice.' tšʾu 'she raises' (G-yqtl 3fs of nšʾ); g 'voice' (cf. Hebrew gārôn). Standard speech-introduction formula.
'[And] she cried: I — yes I — and the mountain…' ʾan 'I' (1cs pronoun emphatic). The emphatic self-assertion of the warrior-goddess.
'I will take a lord(?).' ʾan 'I'; ʾaḫd 'I shall seize' (G-yqtl 1cs of ʾḫd); ʾadn 'lord' (cf. Hebrew ʾādōn).
'…earth(?), she lifts her voice.' ʿrṣ uncertain; possibly 'I will be roused.'
'…I will rest, I will rest in peace.' ʾanḫn 'I will rest, sigh' (G-yqtl 1cs of nḥ; cf. Hebrew nûaḥ); the rest-after-victory formula.
'In my breast (= chest), the throat in my interior.' ʾirty 'my breast' (cf. Hebrew ḥāzeh); npš 'throat, life-breath' (cf. Hebrew nepeš); ḥzr 'inward part, chamber.'

**THE LEVIATHAN-LINE**: 'For I struck Lōtanu the fleeing serpent.' tmḫṣ 'I struck' (G-pf 1cs of mḫṣ; or G-yqtl 2fs 'you struck' — context determines); ltn 'Lōtanu' = Leviathan (cf. Hebrew liwyātān Isa 27:1; Ps 74:14; Job 41); bṯn brḥ 'fleeing serpent' = the same phrase as Isa 27:1 nāḥāš bāriaḥ. MANDATORY CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL — the closest Ugaritic-Hebrew Bible verbal match in the entire corpus.

**THE LEVIATHAN-LINE (continued)**: 'I finished off the writhing serpent.' tkly 'I made an end of' (D-pf 1cs of kly); bṯn ʿqltn 'twisting/writhing serpent' = cf. Isa 27:1 nāḥāš ʿăqallātôn. MANDATORY CROSS-CORPUS: the verbal correspondence with Isa 27:1 is exact.

**THE LEVIATHAN-LINE (continued)**: 'The Tyrant with seven heads.' šlyṭ 'tyrant, ruler' (cf. Hebrew šallîṭ Eccl 8:8); d šbʿt rʾašm 'of seven heads' (cf. Ps 74:14 'You crushed the heads of Leviathan' — pl); cf. Rev 13:1 the seven-headed beast. The cosmic chaos-monster.
'I struck the Beloved-of-ʾIlu, ʾAršayu.' mdd ʾilm 'Beloved of ʾIlu' (= Yammu's epithet, also applied to other chaos-figures); ʾaršy possibly a chaos-deity (= 'Earthly One'?).

i18n.en: [KTU 1.3 col iv: ʿAnatu now travels to Baʿlu's abode on Ṣapunu. The dialogue centers on the central grievance: Baʿlu, though victorious over Yammu, still has no palace befitting his royal status. This complaint sets up the entire palace-building arc that unfolds in KTU 1.4.]

lines.notes: '…the (two) lads are sent.' tlʾakn 'they are sent' (Gt-yqtl 3mp of lʾk; cf. Hebrew malʾāk 'messenger'); ġlmm 'lads' (cf. Hebrew ʿalmâ Gen 24:43).
'…(I) have sent to your son.' lʾakm 'I sent' (G-pf 1cs); bnk 'your son.'
'…(she goes) after Baʿlu.' ʾatr 'after, following' (cf. Hebrew ʾaḥar); the pursuit-of-Baʿlu formula.
'She enters to Baʿlu (on) the heights of Ṣapunu.' tbʾu 'she enters' (G-yqtl 3fs of bwʾ); mrym ṣpn 'heights of Ṣapunu.' ʿAnatu reaches Baʿlu's mountain-palace.
'…through a thousand acres, ten thousand hectares.' The cosmic-distance formula (cf. KTU 1.1 iii 2).
'Baʿlu sees the coming of his sister.' Identical-formula to 1.3 iii 7; the brother-sister recognition-scene.
'The progress of his father's daughter.' Parallel to 1.3 iii 8.
'He sends away wives from before him.' šrḥq 'he makes (them) go far' (Š-impv of rḥq); ʾaṯt 'wives, women.' Baʿlu clears his hall for ʿAnatu — a hospitality-etiquette.
'He places an ox before her.' ʾalp 'ox' (cf. Hebrew ʾeleph); qdmh 'before her.' The hospitality-feast offered to ʿAnatu.
'…a fatling in the midst before her face.' mrʾiʾa 'fatling, choice animal.'
'She returns, she takes her lyre in her hand.' ttb 'she returns' (G-yqtl 3fs of ṯwb); knr 'lyre' (cf. Hebrew kinnôr); the lyre-taking gesture (cf. 1.3 ii 44).
'She sets a wild-bull(?) at her breast.' rʾimt 'wild bull' (cf. Hebrew rĕʾēm Num 23:22) — the bull-on-the-breast image, likely an amulet or pectoral; ʾirt 'breast.'
'She sings (of) the love of Mighty Baʿlu.' tšr 'she sings' (G-yqtl 3fs of šyr); dd 'love, loved-one' (cf. Hebrew dôd 'beloved' Song 1:13). The love-song of ʿAnatu for Baʿlu.
'…the love of Pidray daughter of light.' yd here = 'love' (a homophone of 'hand'; root ydd/wdd 'to love'); cf. 1.3 i 22 for Pidray.
'…the love of Ṭallay daughter of showers.' ʾahbt 'love' (cf. Hebrew ʾahăbâ 'love'); Baʿlu's three daughters now feature in ʿAnatu's song.
'…the love of Arṣayu daughter of Yaʿbudaru.' ʾarṣy 'Arṣay' (the third daughter); yʿbdr possibly her parental ascription.
'[When] the Maiden ʿAnatu [arrived]…' mġy 'arrive' (G-pf of mġy; cf. Hebrew māṣâ — wrong root; properly the Aramaic-related root mġy 'reach'). Arrival-formula.
'…the Sister-in-law of nations arrived.' Parallel restoration.
'He lifts his voice and cries.' The standard speech-introduction formula.
'How (it is) that the Maiden ʿAnatu has arrived?' ʾik 'how, why' (interrogative; cf. Hebrew ʾêk). Baʿlu's greeting/question.
'How (is it that) the Sister-in-law of nations has arrived?' Parallelism.
'Has any enemy risen against Baʿlu?' p 'whether, perhaps' (interrogative particle); ʾib 'enemy' (cf. Hebrew ʾōyēb); yp 'arises'(?). Baʿlu's anxiety-question.
'…(any) adversary to the Cloud-Rider?' ṣrt 'distress, adversary' (cf. Hebrew ṣar 'foe'); rkb ʿrpt 'Cloud-Rider' = Baʿlu's signature epithet.
'Did I not strike the Beloved of ʾIlu, Yammu?' l mḫšt 'I struck' (negative-affirmative; here the rhetorical 'I-indeed-struck'). The victory-recounting.
'Did I not finish off River, the great god?' klt 'I made-an-end of' (D-pf 1cs of kly); rbm 'great' (cf. Hebrew rab).

'I muzzled the Tannin, I bound him up.' tnn 'Tannin, sea-monster' (cf. Hebrew tannîn Gen 1:21; Isa 27:1); ʾištbm 'I muzzled / bound about the mouth' (Št-pf 1cs of šbm). Tannin-defeat alongside Yammu — the chaos-defeating-the-monsters tradition.
'I struck the writhing serpent.' Parallel to 1.3 iii 48 (and Isa 27:1 ʿăqallātôn).
'…the Tyrant with seven heads.' Parallel to 1.3 iii 49. The Leviathan-cluster recurs.
'I struck the Beloved of ʾIlu, ʾArš[a].' Possibly the same chaos-figure as 1.3 iii 50.
'I annihilated the calf of ʾIlu, ʿAtaku.' ʿgl ʾil 'calf of ʾIlu' = a chaos-figure in calf-form; ʿtk possibly 'Old One.'
'I struck Klabt, bitch of the gods, fire.' klbt 'bitch'; ʾišt 'fire' (cf. Hebrew ʾēš) — the fire-demon-as-bitch.
'I finished off the daughter of ʾIlu, Ḏubub (the Flame).' ḏbb 'flame, blaze'; this and the previous line form the chaos-monsters-killed list — ʿAnatu's resumé.
'I fought for silver, I obtained gold.' ʾimtḫṣ 'I fought' (Gt-pf 1cs of mḫṣ); ʾiṯrṯ 'I took possession of' (Gt-pf 1cs of yrṯ; cf. Hebrew yāraš 'inherit'). The post-battle spoil-claim.
'Driven out Baʿlu from the heights of Ṣapunu.' ṭrd 'driven out' (G-pass of ṭrd); Baʿlu's exile-from-Ṣapunu — perhaps a hypothetical the warrior-goddess threatens to undo.
'…(like) a fluttering bird he is chased.' kṣ ʿṣr 'like a bird'; tdy 'she chased' (G-yqtl 3fs of ndy 'to scatter').
'…chariots (are) sent forth.' mrkbt 'chariot' (cf. Hebrew merkābâ); tšlḥm 'they are sent' (Gt). Battle-equipment imagery.
'…(the) mountain, that she be satisfied.' tšbʿ 'she be sated' (G-yqtl 3fs of śbʿ).
'…his city, the bound one(?).' ḥbš 'bound, confined'; lost context.

lines.translit: wn . ʾin . bt . l bʿl . km . ʾilm
lines.notes: **THE CENTRAL COMPLAINT — LENS-RISK SITE**: 'And there is no house for Baʿlu like the gods.' wn 'and indeed' (conjunctive); ʾin 'there is not'; bt 'house, dwelling' (cf. Hebrew bayit); km ʾilm 'like the (other) gods.' THIS IS THE CORE GRIEVANCE that drives the entire palace-building arc of KTU 1.3-1.4. Smith & Pitard 2009 vol 2 pp. 296ff treat this as the thematic hinge of the chapter. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. 2 Sam 7:2 (David: 'I dwell in a house of cedar but the ark dwells in a tent') — the king-without-temple grievance is a structural pattern.

**THE CENTRAL COMPLAINT (continued)**: 'And no court like the sons of ʾAṯirat.' ḥẓr 'court, dwelling-compound' (cf. Hebrew ḥāṣēr); bn ʾaṯrt 'sons of ʾAṯirat' = the 70 sons of the mother-goddess. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: bnê ʾēlîm in the Hebrew Bible (e.g. Ps 29:1).
'(There is) the dwelling of ʾIlu, the canopy of his sons.' mṯb 'dwelling, seat'; mẓll 'shaded place, canopy' (cf. Hebrew ṣēl 'shadow'); the ʾIlu-establishment formula.

'…the dwelling of Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea.' rbt ʾaṯrt ym 'Lady ʾAṯirat (of the) Sea' = the mother-goddess's full title (cf. KTU 1.4 II 28-29). LENS-RISK SITE for Ch 2: the ʾAṯirat-Asherah cross-corpus material (cf. 1 Kgs 18:19; Hadley 2000).
'…the dwelling of Pidray daughter of light.' Baʿlu's daughters listed as already housed in cosmic dwellings (only Baʿlu himself lacks one).
'…the canopy of Ṭallay daughter of showers.'
'…the dwelling of Arṣay daughter of Yaʿbudaru.'
'…the dwelling of the bridal-perfected ones(?).' klt knyt 'consummated brides' (cf. Hebrew kallâ 'bride') — Baʿlu's daughters as 'the perfected brides.'
'[And] ʿAnatu lifted her voice and cried.' Standard speech-introduction.
'(May) ʾIlu the father not be slighted…(?)'. ytʿdd 'he is gathered/strengthened/slighted'; the petitionary mood.
'…will heed his bow, I [...].'

**THE THREAT-FORMULA (preview)**: 'I will make his gray hairs (run) with [blood].' šbt 'old age, gray hair' (cf. Hebrew śêbâ); dmm 'blood' (pl); ʾašhlk 'I will cause to go/flow' (Š-yqtl 1cs of hlk). The famous threat-formula previewed here (full version in 1.3 v 24-25).
**THE THREAT-FORMULA (continued)**: 'His gray-bearded chin with gore.' dqn 'beard, chin' (cf. Hebrew zāqān); mmʿm 'gore' (pl). The shocking-disrespect-to-ʾIlu image.

lines.translit: k l . ytn . bt . l bʿl . km . ʾilm
lines.notes: **THE CORE GRIEVANCE RE-STATED**: 'For he has not given a house to Baʿlu like the gods.' k 'for, because'; l ytn 'he has not given.' ʿAnatu protesting on Baʿlu's behalf.
'[And] no court like the sons of ʾAṯirat.' Parallelism with 1.3 iv 40.
'…spoke ʿAnatu…'. ʿAnatu's speech-ascription.
'…the Maiden ʿAnatu departs.' tbʿ 'she departs' (G-yqtl 3fs of pny/byʿ); ʿAnatu now begins her journey to confront ʾIlu — leading directly into col v.

i18n.en: [KTU 1.3 col v: ʿAnatu arrives at ʾIlu's distant abode (the source of the two rivers, at the springs of the deeps) and delivers her famous threat — that she will trample the patriarch's hoary head if he does not grant Baʿlu a palace. This is the most audacious passage of the divine-assembly material in the Cycle. MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE: feminist scholarship reads ʿAnatu's threat as the audacity of the warrior-goddess within the patriarchal divine structure (Walls 1992; Day 2000 pp. 132-150).]

lines.notes: 'Then indeed she set face…' ʾidk 'then' (cf. Hebrew ʾāz); ytn pnm 'set face toward' — standard travel-formula.

**ʾILU'S ABODE-FORMULA**: 'Toward ʾIlu, (at) the source of the two rivers.' mbk 'source, spring' (cf. Akk. bekû); nhrm 'two rivers' (dual). The famous double-river-source — ʾIlu dwells at the cosmic-spring.

**ʾILU'S ABODE-FORMULA (continued)**: 'In the midst of the channels of the two deeps.' qrb 'midst' (cf. Hebrew qereb); ʾapq 'channel, water-course' (cf. Hebrew ʾāpîq); thmtm 'two deeps' (dual of tĕhôm). The cosmic underworld-spring. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. Gen 2:10 (the river from Eden divided into four heads); the cosmic-spring motif.
'She reaches the abode of ʾIlu.' tgly 'she uncovers, reveals (= reaches by passing through)' (G-yqtl 3fs of gly); ḏd 'abode, pavilion.'

lines.translit: w tbʾu . qrš . mlk . ʾab . šnm
lines.notes: '…and enters the dwelling-tent of the King, the Father of Years.' qrš 'tabernacle, tent-shrine' (cf. Hebrew qereš Exod 26:15); mlk 'King'; ʾab šnm 'Father of Years' = ʾIlu's title — STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. Dan 7:9 ʿattîq yômîn 'Ancient of Days.'

'At the feet of ʾIlu she does not fall.' l tpl 'she does not prostrate' (G-yqtl 3fs negative of npl). **AUDACITY-MARKER**: ʿAnatu refuses the standard prostration-protocol due to a superior deity — extraordinary in the Cycle's poetics. Smith & Pitard 2009 vol 2 pp. 326-330.

'She does not bow down (to) the assembled council.' l tštḥwy 'she does not bow' (Št-yqtl 3fs negative); pḫr mʿd 'congregation of the assembly' (cf. Hebrew sôd, mōʿēd). The refused-prostration to the divine council.
'But the angry princes confront her.' ʾanš 'wrath, anger' (cf. Hebrew ʾānaš); zbym 'princes' (cf. zbl); tngṯnh 'they meet/oppose her' (Gt-yqtl 3mp + 3fs suffix).
'The lads answer, they (= the divine attendants) reply.' ġlmm 'the (two) lads' (divine messengers); yʿnyn 'they answer'(D-yqtl 3mp).
'How has the Maiden ʿAnatu arrived?' The greeting-question (cf. 1.3 iv 20).
'How has the Sister-in-law of nations arrived?'

'Will you smite your fighters of lapis-lazuli?' tmḫṣ 'you smite' (G-yqtl 2fs); mhrh 'his soldiers'; ʾiqnʾi 'lapis-lazuli'(?). Possibly: a warning that ʿAnatu's wrath could turn against ʾIlu's own retinue.
'…she destroys his seven lads.' tṣmt 'she annihilates' (G-yqtl 3fs of ṣmt); šbʿt 'seven'; ġlm 'lads, attendants.' The threat of slaughtering the divine entourage.
'…she leaves indignant, the [Mai]den ʿAnatu departs.' qnʾi possibly 'with jealous-zeal' (cf. Hebrew qinʾâ); the leave-taking with stored-up anger.
'(But) she lowers herself at the feet of ʾIlu.' tšpl 'she lowers herself, makes-low' (G-yqtl 3fs of špl; cf. Hebrew šāpēl). The grudging compliance now — but the threat is coming.
'…the word from his nose(?).' Possibly: word of nose-anger (cf. Hebrew ʾap 'nose, anger').
'(That) Baʿlu the Living(?) may take…' bʿl ḥy 'living Baʿlu' — possibly a vocative-praise.
'…I will return.' ʾib 'enemy'; ʾank 'I' — the ambiguous threat.
'And the Maiden ʿAnatu answered.' Standard speech-ascription.
'The Sister-in-law of nations replied.' Parallel.

lines.translit: tḥm . k tḥmm . hwt . k hwt . ʾaḫrṣ
lines.notes: '(Hear my) message as messages, my word as the word I will hasten…' tḥm 'message' (cf. KTU 1.3 iii 23); ʾaḫrṣ 'I will hasten' (Š-yqtl 1cs of rṣ; cf. Hebrew rûṣ).
'Listen to my word, ʾIlu the King.' tbn 'listen, understand' (G-yqtl 2ms of byn); the address-to-the-patriarch.

'You who begot me — a word that I will (now) speak.' d ynnk 'you who fathered me' (G-pf 3ms + 1cs suffix of ynn; possibly 'you are my begetter'). ʿAnatu invokes her filial relationship to ʾIlu (she is his daughter) — the audacity is doubled by the kinship-claim.

**THE THREAT — MANDATORY MAJOR**: 'I will make your gray hairs (run) with blood!' ʾašhlk 'I will cause (it) to flow' (Š-yqtl 1cs of hlk); šbt h 'his gray hair / old age' (cf. Hebrew śêbâ); dmm 'with blood.' The audacious threat to the patriarch. Smith & Pitard 2009 vol 2 pp. 332ff. LENS-RISK SITE: ʿAnatu, a female deity, threatens the head of the pantheon.

**THE THREAT (continued) — MANDATORY MAJOR**: 'Your gray-bearded chin with gore!' dqn 'beard, chin' (cf. Hebrew zāqān 'old man, bearded one'); mmʿm 'with gore.' The descent-into-bodily-violation of the highest divine figure. Cf. Walls 1992 *The Goddess Anat in Ugaritic Myth* pp. 173-185.

lines.translit: w yʿn . lṭpn . ʾil . d pʾid
lines.notes: 'And the Benevolent ʾIlu the kind-hearted answered.' lṭpn ʾil d pʾid = ʾIlu's full epithet-formula. ʾIlu's reply now.

'I know you, that you are stubborn(?).' ydʿtk 'I know you' (G-pf 1cs + 2fs suffix of ydʿ; cf. Hebrew yādaʿ); ʾanšt 'you are wrathful / fierce' (G-pf 2fs of ʾnš). ʾIlu acknowledges ʿAnatu's character without rebuking the threat — the patriarch yields gracefully.

lines.translit: k l . ʾiṯ . b ʾilht . qlṣk
lines.notes: 'For there is not among the goddesses one (so) bold as you.' qlṣ 'derision, boldness' (cf. Hebrew qālas Ezek 22:5); the recognition-of-uniqueness. ʿAnatu is THE warrior-goddess.
'What do you desire, O Maiden ʿAnatu?' tʾaršn 'you desire, request' (G-yqtl 2fs of ʾrš; cf. Hebrew ʾāraš 'to betroth/request'). ʾIlu invites her petition — the threat has worked.
'What do you request, O Sister-in-law of nations?'
'And the Maiden ʿAnatu answered.'
'(My) request — that Mighty Baʿlu may rejoice(?).' tḥm 'message, request'; ywd possibly 'he may know' or 'he may rejoice.' The petition opens with a wish-formula.
'…that you arrange (it for) Prince Baʿlu of the earth.' tʿrk 'you arrange / set in order' (D-yqtl 2ms of ʿrk; cf. Hebrew ʿārak).
'…(that he) place (his) bull in (the place of) the heavens (he will) erect.' Building-action-vocabulary.
'Mighty Baʿlu like the gods!' = like the other gods who have palaces. The core grievance restated as a wish.
'[And] the Benevolent ʾIlu the kind-hearted answered.'
'…I (am)…servant of ʾIlu(?).' Lost portion; possibly ʾIlu's deflection or partial commitment.
'…the king, ʾIlu, Dagan…'. Fragmentary.
'…mountain of silver…' Cosmic-construction-vocabulary.
'…in fields(?).'
'…ʾAṯirat…' — the introduction of the next mover. ʿAnatu's confrontation has failed to secure the palace directly from ʾIlu; the petition must now go through ʾAṯirat (mother of the gods).
'…I will speak(?).'
'…she sends…'
'…Baʿlu…'
'…Ṣapunu…'

i18n.en: [KTU 1.3 col vi: heavily damaged in places; the surviving text shows ʿAnatu reporting back to Baʿlu and the embassy being sent to Kothar-wa-Khasis (the divine craftsman) in his Mediterranean abodes of Kaphtor and Memphis. This closes KTU 1.3 and sets up the construction-arc of KTU 1.4.]

lines.notes: **THE WINDOW-FORMULA (preview)**: '…I shall set a window in the palace(s).' ʾašt 'I will place' (G-yqtl 1cs of šty); ʾurbt 'window, lattice' (cf. Hebrew ʾărubbâ Gen 7:11 'windows of heaven'); bhtm 'palaces.' The famous window-debate previewed; full development at KTU 1.4 vii 14-30. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: Gen 7:11 ʾărubbôt haššāmayim 'windows of heaven.'
'[A skylight in the midst of] the temple.' ḥlln 'lattice-skylight'; qrb 'midst'; hklm 'temple' (cf. Hebrew hêkāl).
'[And Mighty Baʿlu answered].' Restoration of the standard speech-formula.
'…[I will] take the gods [of heaven].' ʾaḫd 'I will seize' (G-yqtl 1cs).
'…until the tables.' Banquet-vocabulary fragment.
'The gods eat and drink.' ṯlḥm 'eat' (G-impv mp of lḥm); tšty 'drink' (G-yqtl 3fp of šty). The standard divine-banquet-formula.
'…give (food) to the young, light…'. tn 'give' (G-impv); llʾim 'young, kids'; ʾar 'light, milk-young'(?).
'[And] the lads (= messengers) answer, they reply.' Standard messenger-reply formula.
'…tablets of the message of [Baʿ]lu.' lḫt 'tablet' (cf. Hebrew lûaḥ); the written-message variant.
'…they depart.' ttbʿn (Gt-yqtl 3mp of tbʿ/pny).
'They set face toward Kothar.' kṯr 'Kothar (-wa-Khasis)' = the divine craftsman. The Kothar-embassy now.
'(To) Memphis, the god of all (it).' ḥkpt 'Memphis' (= Ḥwt-kʾ-Ptḥ 'House-of-the-ka-of-Ptaḥ'); the Egyptian-abode of Kothar.
'Kaphtor (= Crete) the t[hrone of his seat].' Standard Kothar-abode-formula (cf. KTU 1.1 iii 1). Crete + Egypt as the divine craftsman's twin domain.
'[Memphis, the land of his inheritance].' Restored parallel.
'In a thousand acres, ten thousand hectares.' Cosmic-distance formula.

lines.translit: l pʿn . kṯr . hbr . w q[l]
lines.notes: 'At the feet of Kothar bow and fa[ll]…'. The standard prostration-formula now addressed to Kothar — the divine craftsman receives respect.
'…prostrate yourselves and honor him.' The four-verb prostration-formula completion.
'(Now) speak to Kothar-wa-Khasis.' Standard message-delivery-formula.

lines.translit: ṯny . l hyn . d ḥrš . ydm
lines.notes: 'Repeat to Hayin of the (two) skilled hands.' hyn 'Hayin' = Kothar's other name; d ḥrš ydm 'the one of skilled hands' (cf. KTU 1.1 iii 4-5).
'Message of Mighty Baʿlu.'
'Word of the Mighty One of warriors.' (cf. KTU 1.3 iii 23-24).
**THE BUILDING-COMMISSION**: '…quickly, palaces will be built.' hš 'quickly, hasten'; bhtm tbnn 'palaces will be built' (G-pass yqtl of bny; cf. Hebrew bānâ). The construction-commission to Kothar.
'[Quickly, will-be-erected] temples.' trmmn 'will be erected' (passive); hklm 'temples.' The standard palace-construction-formula (cf. KTU 1.1 iii 27).
'…honor him…'
'…Kothar…'

i18n.en: [KTU 1.4 col i: a transition-column. The opening describes the absence of a palace befitting Baʿlu, repeating elements of the earlier complaint. The column then narrates the preparation of gifts (precious metals) for ʾAṯirat, who must intercede with ʾIlu. KTU 1.4 is the longest single tablet of the Cycle (~410 lines across 8 columns).]

lines.translit: k l . ytn . bt . l bʿl . km . ʾilm
lines.notes: **THE CORE COMPLAINT — RECURRING**: 'For he has not given a house to Baʿlu like the gods.' The hinge-complaint of 1.3 iv 39, 52 now restated. (cf. Smith & Pitard 2009 vol 2 pp. 391-400.)
'And no court like the sons of ʾAṯirat.'
'(But) the dwelling of ʾIlu, the canopy of his sons.'
'…the dwelling of Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea.'
'…the dwelling of Pidray daughter of light.'
'…the canopy of Ṭallay daughter of showers.'
'…the dwelling of Arṣay daughter of Yaʿbudaru.'
'…the dwelling of the perfected brides.' (= Baʿlu's three daughters, now properly housed.)

**THE METAL-CASTING SCENE**: 'He pours silver, he casts gold.' yṣq 'he pours, smelts' (G-yqtl of yṣq; cf. Hebrew yāṣaq 'to cast metal' Exod 25:12). The preparation of precious metals — the gift-set for ʾAṯirat.
'He pours silver by the thousands.' l ʾalpm 'by thousands' — bulk metallurgy.
'(And) gold he pours out by the ten-thousands.' rbbt 'ten-thousands' (= myriads).
'He pours (a) tent / pavilion(?).' ḥym possibly 'pavilion, encampment'; tbṯ uncertain.
'…like silver.'
'She sets…mountain of silver.'
'…gold.'
'A youth…ʾIlu, ʾAṯirat.'
'…her standing-place…'
'…like gold in the hand of the craftsman.'
'…the structure of peace-offerings.' šlmm 'peace-offerings' (cf. Hebrew šĕlāmîm Lev 7:11).
'…the king himself.'
'…he slaughters oxen.' Cf. the standard banquet-formula.
'…also sheep.' Continuing the sacrificial-list.
'[Bulls and] fatlings.'
'[Rams, calves] of a year.'
'[Lambs, an abundance of] kids.'
'…bow and fall…' The prostration-formula introducing Kothar's audience.
'…[prostr]ate yourselves and honor him.'
'He pours…sons of the clouds.'
'…Kothar.'
'Upon the(two) knees he arranges the (his) face.' brktm 'knees' (cf. Hebrew berek).
'[And he pours] a krpn-bowl in both hands.' Cup-handling formula.
'…the hero of good voice sings.' Cf. 1.3 i 19.
'…(in) the presence of Baʿlu on the heights of Ṣapunu.'
'[Baʿlu behol]ds…'
'…Baʿlu sees.'
'…he gives his bow.'
'…ʾAṯirat.'
'…sons.'
'…silver.'
'…he answers.'
'…craftsman.'
'…Kothar.'

i18n.en: [KTU 1.4 col ii: the scene shifts to ʾAṯirat, Lady of the Sea (rbt ʾaṯrt ym), at her coastal abode. She is engaged in textile-work (spinning) when she sees Baʿlu and ʿAnatu approaching with gifts. MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE: this is the most extended treatment of ʾAṯirat (the mother-goddess of the Ugaritic pantheon) in any Late-Bronze Northwest-Semitic text. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS for 1 Kgs 18:19 (the prophets of Asherah); the Asherah-polemic in Israelite religion (Day 2000 pp. 42-67; Olyan 1988; Hadley 2000).]

lines.notes: 'She takes her spindle [in her hand].' plk 'spindle' (cf. Hebrew pelek 2 Sam 3:29; Prov 31:19). ʾAṯirat at her textile-work — a domestic-divine image.
'A spindle of l[oad in] her right hand.' tʿlt 'load, weight'; ymn 'right hand.' The textile-imagery continues.
'Her garment, the covering of her fl[esh].' mks 'covering, garment' (cf. Hebrew kĕsût); bšr 'flesh' (cf. Hebrew bāśār).
'…she descends(?) into the sea.' tmt possibly 'she casts/descends' — ʾAṯirat's connection to the sea-shore.
'…she scoops up…'
'…like a vine(?), seven.'
'…she pours like draw-women(?).' šibm possibly 'cattle-drivers' or 'water-drawers' (cf. šʾb).
'She lights/kindles in (her) hand.' tʿpp possibly 'she makes-flutter / kindles' (D-yqtl 3fs).
'She raises her eyes and beholds.' ʿn 'eye' (cf. Hebrew ʿayin). The vision-formula.
'(From) the deeps she raises her voice and cries.' tšʾu gh 'she lifts her voice' (standard speech-introduction).
'Ho[w] (is it that) Mighty Baʿlu has come?' Greeting-question (cf. 1.3 iv 20).
'Ho[w] (is it that) the Maiden ʿAnatu has come?'
'My slayers, or the slayers of my sons?' mḫṣy 'my smiters'; hm 'or'; bny 'my sons' (= the 70 sons of ʾAṯirat). The mother-of-the-gods's first thought is for her children.
'[O]r the destroyers of the kin of (my) clan.' mkly 'destroyers' (Pi-pl); ṣbrt 'group, clan'; ʾary 'kin, kinsman.' The maternal concern for her divine offspring.
'A staff/sceptre, she arranges, Yaʿbudar(?).' ḫṯʾi 'staff, club' (cf. Akk. ḫuṭāru).
'…lapis-lazuli (gifts), she rejoices.' ʾiqnʾim 'lapis-lazuli pieces'; tšmḫ 'she rejoices' (G-yqtl 3fs of šmḫ; cf. Hebrew śāmaḥ). ʾAṯirat now sees the bridal-gifts.
'…now silver of ʾAṯirat(?).' Wedding-gift inventory.
'…workmanship of silver, also gold.'
'Rejoice[s] the Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea.' Confirming her positive reception.
'Aloud to her lad she cries.' gm 'aloud'; ġlm 'lad, attendant' — ʾAṯirat addresses her divine attendant. Her primary attendant is Qadeš-wa-ʾAmrar.
'See the (one of) skilled-handicraft of the fields(?).' Possibly addressed to the lad.
'…fisherman of the Lady.' dġy 'fisherman' (cf. Hebrew dawwāg) — one of ʾAṯirat's coastal-deity titles is connected with fishing.
'…ʾAṯirat of the Sea.'
'Take a net in your hand.' rṯ 'net' (cf. Hebrew rešet); the fishing-vocabulary.
'…(the) Lady upon the hands.'
'…of the Beloved of ʾIlu, Yammu.' The mdd ʾil 'Beloved of ʾIlu' epithet here — Yammu is invoked as ʾAṯirat's sphere of association.
'[In] Yammu, River, the great god.' Identifying Yammu/Nahar — ʾAṯirat's sea-domain.
'…Yaʿbudar.'
'Give seven…' šbʿ 'seven'; an offering-count.
'…they are sent.'
'…she rejoiced.'
'…like a vineyard.'
'…clarity / there is(?).'
'Comes…' (recipient).
'The progress of [B]aʿlu.'
'…(s)he stands.'
'…Lady.'
'…rejoiced.'
'…in dust.'
'…she slays(?).'
'…he pours.'
'…GLN.'
'…in silver.'
'…give (an) ox.'
'…Gpn (= Vine-deity, Baʿlu's messenger).'
'…Kothar.'
'…rejoice.'
'…sea.'

i18n.en: [KTU 1.4 col iii: Baʿlu and ʿAnatu present their case to ʾAṯirat, requesting her intercession with ʾIlu. The dialogue between the mother-goddess and the storm-god is one of the more intimate political exchanges of the Cycle.]

lines.notes: 'But the angry princes (= attendants) confront…' Cf. 1.3 v 8.
'…Baʿlu, the noble ones confront…'
'They cut … departing, they ascend.' Movement-vocabulary.
'[Arrives] Mighty Baʿlu.'
'[Arr]ives the Maiden ʿAnatu.' The dual-arrival to ʾAṯirat's abode.
'They prostrate themselves (to) the Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea.' tṯpln 'they prostrate' (Gt-yqtl 3mp of npl 'to fall'). The protocol-prostration to the mother-goddess.

'They honor the Creatress of the gods.' tkbdn 'they honor' (D-yqtl 3mp + n-ending); qnyt ʾilm 'Creatress (acquirer/owner) of the gods' = ʾAṯirat's standard epithet (cf. Hebrew qōnâ 'create/acquire' Gen 14:19, 22). STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: qōnê šāmayim wāʾāreṣ 'creator of heaven and earth' — ʾAṯirat's creator-title is THE closest Late-Bronze cognate to Genesis.
'Indeed, her dwelling is lapis-lazu[li].' ʾiqnʾim 'lapis-lazuli' — the precious-stone-dwelling of ʾAṯirat.
'[And] the Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea answered.'
'How has Mighty Baʿlu come?'
'How has the Maiden ʿAnatu come?'
'My slayers, or the slayers of my sons?' (Cf. 1.4 ii 15.)
'Or the destroyers of the kin of my clan?'
'[And] the Maiden ʿAnatu answered.'
'O Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea!' Vocative-address.
'Two words I shall speak.' ṯn 'two'; rgmm 'words.' The two-fold speech-formula.
'A third I shall repeat to you.' ṯlṯt 'third'; ʾaṯnyk 'I shall repeat' (Dt-yqtl 1cs + 2fs suffix).
'For verily I have made-an-end of(?).' krty possibly 'in my hand'; ʾašṣmt = Š-pf 1cs of ṣmt 'destroy.'
'Where (is) Dagan(?), the gracious-one of Baʿlu?' ʾiy 'where' (cf. Hebrew ʾay); the question-formula. pid 'kindness' (= the same root as d pʾid 'kind-hearted').
'[For] he has not given a house to Baʿlu.' THE CORE COMPLAINT to ʾAṯirat directly.
'[Like the g]ods, court like the sons of ʾAṯirat.' Repetition of the central grievance.
'[The] dwelling of ʾIlu, the canopy of his sons.'
'[The] dwelling of Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea.'
'…the dwelling of Pidray daughter of light.'
'…the canopy of Ṭallay daughter of showers.'
'…the dwelling of Arṣay daughter of Yaʿbudaru.'
'…the dwelling of the perfected brides.'
'And the Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea answered.'
'…she rejoices(?), if not.'
'…I will take/accept.'
'…in the hand of Bull ʾIlu my father.'
'…she rejoices.'
'…heavens (of) oil.' šmm 'heavens'; šmnt 'fatness, abundance' (cf. Hebrew šemen).
'…they/she serve(s) food.'
'…he drinks.'
'…wine.'

i18n.en: [KTU 1.4 col iv: ʾAṯirat now sets out, ridden by her loyal attendant Qadeš-wa-ʾAmrar, to the distant abode of ʾIlu at the source of the rivers. This is one of the longest journey-scenes in the Cycle. The protocol of arrival, prostration, and welcome is described in full detail. ʾIlu greets ʾAṯirat with intimate language.]

lines.notes: '…she follows the sea.' ʾaṯry 'her path'(?).
'The Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea exults.' tḥdy 'she rejoices' (G-yqtl 3fs of ḥdy).
'Aloud to her lad she cries.' gm 'aloud'; the call to her attendant.
'See the skilled-craftsman of the fields(?).' Possibly addressed to Qadeš-wa-ʾAmrar.
'…fisherman of the Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea.'
'Qadeš takes the saddle(?).' qdš 'Qadeš' (= ʾAṯirat's primary attendant Qadeš-wa-ʾAmrar 'Holy-and-Mighty').'
'ʾAmrar like a star before (her).' ʾamrr 'ʾAmrar'; k kbkb 'like a star' — the divine-attendant lighting the way. Cf. the messenger-star imagery; possibly cognate to Hebrew kôkāb.
'After the Maiden ʿAnatu.'
'And Baʿlu departs (to) the heights of Ṣapunu.'
'Then indeed she set face…' Travel-formula opening.
'…toward ʾIlu, (at) the source of the two rivers.'
'…in the midst of the channels of the two deeps.'
'She reaches the abode of ʾIlu, and enters.'
'…the dwelling-tent of the King, the Father of Years.'

lines.translit: l pʿn . ʾil . thbr . w tql
lines.notes: 'At the feet of ʾIlu she bows and falls down.' thbr 'she bows' (G-yqtl 3fs of hbr); tql 'she falls' (G-yqtl 3fs of npl). The standard prostration-formula — ʾAṯirat, unlike ʿAnatu, observes protocol.
'She prostrates herself and honors him.' The four-verb prostration-formula completed.
'When ʾIlu beholds her…' hlm 'when' (temporal particle); yphnh 'he sees her' (G-yqtl 3ms + 3fs suffix of phy/pny). Note: phy is the rare 'see' root cognate to Hebrew pānâ (turn face).

'He cracks/opens his jaw and laughs.' yprq 'he splits / opens' (G-yqtl 3ms of prq; cf. Akk. parāqu); lṣb 'jaw, mouth-corner'; yṣḥq 'he laughs' (G-yqtl 3ms of ṣḥq; cf. Hebrew ṣāḥaq Gen 17:17). ʾIlu's delight at ʾAṯirat's arrival — the laugh-of-recognition between divine consorts.
'He places his feet on the footstool.' yṯpd 'he sets, plants' (G-yqtl 3ms of ṯpd); hdm 'footstool' (cf. Hebrew hădōm Ps 110:1).
'…and snaps his fingers.' yqrṣ 'he snaps, pinches' (G-yqtl of qrṣ); ʾuṣbʿt 'fingers.' A gesture of pleased attention.
'He lifts his voice and cries.'
**ʾILU'S INTIMATE GREETING**: 'How has the Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea come?' ʾIlu's standard greeting-question now to his own consort.

**ʾILU'S INTIMATE GREETING (continued)**: 'How have you come, O Creatress of the gods?' ʾatwt 'you have come' (G-pf 2fs of ʾtw/ʾty; cf. Hebrew ʾātâ); qnyt ʾilm 'Creatress of the gods.' The double-greeting marks the spousal-bond.
'Are you very hungry, having traveled(?)?' rġb 'be hungry' (G-stative); the welcome-host's hospitality-question.
'Or very thirsty?' ġmʾi 'be thirsty' (G-stative of ġmʾ; cf. Akk. ṣamû). The hospitality-couplet hunger // thirst.
'Eat, or drink!' lḥm 'eat!' (G-impv); štym 'drink!' (G-impv mp/du).
'Eat from the tables, eat!'
'Drink wine from the krpn-bowls.'
'From the golden cup, the blood of trees.' Cf. 1.3 i 4.
'If perhaps the love of King ʾIlu has stirred you…' yd 'love' (= the same homophone of yad); yḥssk 'stirs you, arouses you' (D-yqtl 3ms + 2fs suffix). The sexual-marital invitation.
'…(if) the love of the Bull excites you…' ʾahbt 'love' (cf. Hebrew ʾahăbâ); tʿrrk 'arouses you' (D-yqtl 3fs + 2fs suffix). The mutual-arousal formula.
'And the Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea answered.'
'Your word, ʾIlu, is wise.' ḥkm 'wise' (cf. Hebrew ḥākām). The diplomatic-flattery opening.
'Your wisdom is with eternity.' ʿm ʿlm 'with eternity' = perpetually-wise. ḥkm + ʿlm = the wisdom-eternity pair.
'…life, good fortune (is) your word.'
'Your word, ʾIlu, is wise.'
'…(but) the king(ship) of Mighty Baʿlu (concerns me).'
'…(let him be) our judge, and there is none above him.' ṯpṭn 'our judge' (cf. Hebrew šôpēṭēnû). The kingship-acknowledgement.
'…all of us(?) (bring) gift…'
'…all of us (bring) tribute.' nbl 'tribute, dedication' (cf. Hebrew nēbel).
'…cup of being / sphere(?).'
'[And ʾIlu answered].'
'…I, ʿAnatu(?).'
'[Am I, then, a slave?] A slave of ʾAṯirat?' ʿbd 'slave, servant'; ʾank 'I' — ʾIlu's possible rhetorical question rejecting subservience.
'…of (the) handmaid(?).' Possibly a maidservant-reference.
'…you fashion / craft.'
'…brick / building-block.' lbnt 'brick' (cf. Hebrew lĕbēnâ Exod 1:14); building-vocabulary previewing the construction-scene.
'…we shall give-gift (to) her.' mġnn 'to placate with gifts' (cf. Hebrew māgēn 'shield').
'…the Maiden ʿAnatu answers.'
'…the gift of you(?).'
'…the death of me / death I (am)(?).'
'…years I have(?).'
'…Kaphtor.'
'…(no) house for Baʿlu.' THE CORE GRIEVANCE recurs.
'…like the gods.'
'…the kingship of the Mighty One.'
'…(of) Baʿlu, dove(?).'
'…the hand of ʾIlu.'
'…she descends(?).'

i18n.en: [KTU 1.4 col v: ʾAṯirat presents the petition formally; ʾIlu grants permission for Baʿlu's palace to be built. This is the most important divine-council decision of the entire Cycle. Kothar-wa-Khasis is summoned, and construction-planning begins. MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE: the divine-council permission-grant pattern (cf. 1 Kgs 22:19-22 the council of heaven; Job 1:6-12; Isa 6).]

lines.notes: '…words I shall take from you.' ʾaqḥnk 'I shall accept' (G-yqtl 1cs + 2fs/sg suffix of lqḥ).
'A [thi]rd I shall repeat to you.'
**ʾILU GRANTS PERMISSION — MANDATORY MAJOR**: '[And] the Benevolent [ʾIlu] the kind-hearted [answered]…'. The pivotal divine-decision-formula. LENS-RISK SITE: the divine-council grant pattern.
'…if seven years…' šbʿ šnt 'seven years' — possibly the temporal frame of the construction. Cf. 1 Kgs 6:38 (Solomon's temple built in seven years).
'[Eight, or fi]ve years.' The temporal-pair formula.

lines.translit: [...] tn . bt . l b[ʿl . km . ʾilm]
lines.notes: **THE GRANTING-DECREE**: '[Let it be given,] a house to Ba[ʿlu like the gods]!' tn 'give!' (G-impv). THE LONG-AWAITED PERMISSION-GRANT — the core decree.
'[And] court like the sons of ʾAṯirat.'
'[And] the Lady ʾAṯirat of the Sea answered.'
'Great are the gods in wisdom.' rbt 'great'; ḥkmt 'wisdom' (cf. Hebrew ḥokmâ). ʾAṯirat's praise.

**THE GRAY-BEARD PRAISE**: 'Your gray-beard truly teaches you.' šbt 'gray-hair'; dqn 'beard'; tsrk 'instructs you' (G-yqtl 3fs of ysr; cf. Hebrew yāsar 'to discipline, instruct'). The gray-beard-as-wisdom-marker — inversion of ʿAnat's threat at 1.3 v 24-25 (there the gray hairs were to be bloodied; here they are praised as wise).
'…the whisper of your tongue…' lḫš 'whisper'; lšn 'tongue' (cf. Hebrew lāšôn).
'…(at) the rising of(?)…'
'…the heavens are stretched / pinch(?).' qrṣ 'pinch, stretch, fashion' — possibly the cosmic-creation-vocabulary (cf. Hebrew qāraṣ Job 33:6).
'…I shall acquire kingship(?).'
'…house for Baʿlu.'
'[Li]ke the gods.'
'And court like the sons of ʾAṯirat.'
'…the Maiden ʿAnatu rejoices.' tšmḫ — the moment of victory.

**ʿANAT'S JOY-DANCE — STRONG IMAGE**: 'She stamps her feet and shakes the earth.' tdʿṣ 'she stamps' (G-yqtl 3fs of dʿṣ — kicking, stamping); pʿnm 'feet'; tr 'shake, set-quivering' (G-yqtl 3fs of twr; cf. Hebrew tērû 'tremble'?). Earth-shaking joy — note the parallel to Baʿlu's voice 'shaking the earth' at 1.4 vii 32, and the wider theophany-vocabulary (Ps 18:8 'the earth quaked').
'Then indeed she set face…' Travel-formula now for ʿAnatu's race to bring the news to Baʿlu.
'…toward Baʿlu (on) the heights of Ṣapunu.'
'…through a thousand acres, ten thousand hectares.'
'The Maiden ʿAnatu laughs.' ṣḥq 'she laughs' (G-pf 3fs of ṣḥq; cf. Hebrew ṣāḥaq Gen 21:6 Sarah's laugh). The joy of the victorious news-bearer.
'She lifts her voice and cries.'

**ʿANAT'S NEWS — JUBILANT**: 'Let me give Baʿlu glad-tidings, for never (again) shall (the matter) be raised(?).' tbšrny 'announce-good-news to me / let me announce' (D-yqtl 1cs of bšr; cf. Hebrew biśśar 'to bring good news'); the verb of evangel.
'(There) shall be given to him a house, for [...]'
'…ʾAṯirat sends.'
'The son of Dagan (= Baʿlu) — ʾArṭanu of love.' bn dgn 'son of Dagan' = Baʿlu's standard patronymic; dd 'love.'
'A house for Baʿlu like the gods!' The granting-decree restated triumphally.
'A court like the sons of ʾAṯirat!'
'And Mighty Baʿlu rejoices.'
'Cry out: A craftsman in your palace!' ṣḥ 'cry!' (G-impv); ḥrn 'craftsman, fashioner' — Kothar's role-title.
'A handicraft-master in the midst of your temple.' ʿdbt 'arrangement, set-up'; qrb hklk 'midst of your temple.'
**THE COSMIC-MATERIAL FORMULA**: 'May the mountains bring you abundance of silver…' tblk 'may they bring to you' (G-yqtl 3mp + 2ms suffix of ybl); ġrm 'mountains'; mʾid 'abundance.'

'…the hills, the desire of gold.' gbʿm 'hills' (cf. Hebrew gibʿâ); mḥmd 'precious, desire' (cf. Hebrew maḥmād). The cosmic-resource-bringing formula. Cf. Ps 95:4 ('in his hand are the depths of the earth, and the mountain-peaks are his').
'…may there bring you the choice (of) the deeps(?).' ʾudr 'choice, select'; ʾilqṣm uncertain (possibly 'gold-rivers' or 'extremities').
**THE PALACE-MATERIALS**: '…build a palace of silver and gold.' bn (= bny) 'build!' (G-impv); bht 'palace.' The silver-and-gold palace specification.
'A palace of pure lapis-lazuli.' ṭhrm 'pure' (cf. Hebrew ṭāhôr); ʾiqnʾim 'lapis-lazuli.' Three-mineral construction: silver, gold, lapis.
'I will hasten / I rejoice; the Maiden ʿAnatu (rejoices).' Joy-finale.
'…(she) sets, gift she dons.' tlbš 'she clothes' (G-yqtl 3fs of lbš; cf. Hebrew lābaš).
'…she stamps (her) feet.' Joy-dance repeats.
'…and shakes the earth.' Recurring.
'…upon the face of…'
'…she sends.'
'…messengers.' mlʾakm 'messengers' (cf. Hebrew malʾāk; Ugaritic lʾk 'to send').
'…unto Kothar-wa-Khasis.' The Kothar-summons.
'…a robe / clothing.'
'…she sends.'
'…Kothar.'
'…the house of Baʿlu.'
'…will be completed.'
'…seven days.' šbʿt ymm 'seven days' — the construction-period unit (preview to 1.4 vi-vii).

**THE CEDARS-OF-LEBANON**: '…cedar in Lebanon.' ʾrz 'cedar' (cf. Hebrew ʾerez); lbnn 'Lebanon.' STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: the cedars-of-Lebanon construction-material (cf. 1 Kgs 5:13ff. Solomon's temple from Lebanon-cedar; Ps 104:16). This is a literal-shared building-material between Late-Bronze Ugarit and Iron-Age Israel.
'…the building of Baʿlu.'
'…Kothar.'
'…house.'
'…they are sent / served.'
'…Kothar arrives.'

i18n.en: [KTU 1.4 col vi: Kothar-wa-Khasis arrives at Baʿlu's Ṣapunu and begins the construction of the palace. Baʿlu personally directs the work; cedar, silver, gold and lapis-lazuli are gathered. The fire-firing of the palace (the architectural-firing of mud-brick) takes seven days. MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE: cosmic-temple-building parallels with 1 Kgs 5-8 (Solomon's temple), Ezek 40-48 (the visionary temple), Exod 25-31, 35-40 (the tabernacle). See Hurowitz 1992 'I Have Built You an Exalted House.']

lines.notes: 'Kothar-wa-Khasis arrived.'
'…Baʿlu laughs from above(?).'
'He takes silver in his hand.' The cup-and-tool gesture of the host.
'Gold he pours by the thousands.'
'He pours dust like(?) his name(?).' Possibly: 'he casts a mold (of) earth as is his manner.' ʿpr 'dust, earth' (cf. Hebrew ʿāpār) — the mud-brick foundation.
'Arranged like a vineyard, krpn-vessels.' Arrangement of the construction-banquet.
'The building of my temple.' bnyt 'construction' (verbal noun of bny); hkly 'my temple' (cf. Hebrew hêkālî).
'And Kothar-wa-Khasis answered.'
'Hear, O Mighty Baʿlu!' šmʿ 'hear!' (G-impv; cf. Hebrew šĕmaʿ Deut 6:4).
'Listen, O Cloud-Rider!' bn 'understand, give-ear' (G-impv of byn).

**THE FAMOUS WINDOW DEBATE — MANDATORY MAJOR (Kothar's question)**: 'Shall I not place a window in the palac[e]?' bl 'shall not, surely' (interrogative-affirmative); ʾašt 'I will set' (G-yqtl 1cs of šty); ʾurbt 'window, lattice' (cf. Hebrew ʾărubbâ Gen 7:11, 8:2; Mal 3:10). STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: the ʾărubbâ in Gen 7:11 'windows of heaven' is THE cognate. The window-debate is one of the most discussed scenes in the entire Baal Cycle (Smith & Pitard 2009 vol 2 pp. 605-624).

**THE WINDOW DEBATE (continued)**: 'A skylight in the midst of the temple.' ḥlln 'skylight, opening' (cf. Akk. ḫullānu); qrb 'midst.' The 'window in the temple' is COSMIC: through the window the storm-god's voice (rain, thunder) goes forth into the world.
'[And] Mighty Baʿlu [answered].'

**BAʿLU REFUSES THE WINDOW — MANDATORY MAJOR**: 'Do not place a window in the [palace]!' ʾal 'do not!' (negative imperative; cf. Hebrew ʾal). Baʿlu refuses the window — the reason emerges in the next lines.
'A skylight [in the midst of the temple].'
'…(if) the love of P[idray daughter of light]…'
'…(of) Ṭallay daughter of showers.'

**BAʿLU'S REASON — LENS-RISK SITE**: '…(lest) the Beloved of ʾI[lu, Yammu]…'. mdd ʾil ym 'Yammu Beloved of ʾIlu' — the reason Baʿlu fears a window: Yammu (the Sea, now defeated but ever-threatening) might steal in through the open window. The cosmic-water-from-above threatening through the window-of-heaven; cf. Gen 7:11 'all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the windows of heaven were opened.' MANDATORY CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL.
'…they will deride/jeer.' yqlṣn 'they will mock' (G-yqtl + n-ending; cf. Hebrew qālas).
'He will dispute(?).'
'Cry out: a craftsman in the palace(s)!'
'…handicraft in the midst of the te[mple].'
'May the mountains bring you abundance of silver.' (Cf. 1.4 v 36.)
'The hills, the desire of gold.'
'May they bring you choice (of) (treasures).'

lines.translit: w bn . bht . ksp . w ḫrṣ
lines.notes: 'And build a palace of silver and gold.'
'A palace of pure lapis-lazuli.'
'Mighty Baʿlu rejoices.'

**THE SEVEN-DAY FIRING — STRONG IMAGE**: 'Seven days the [fire] burns…'. tʿrm 'they kindle' (D-yqtl); ʾišt 'fire' (cf. Hebrew ʾēš). The famous seven-day fire-firing of the palace (= the brick-kiln-firing of the construction). Cf. 1 Kgs 6:38 (Solomon's temple built in seven years); but here it is the firing-period, not the total construction.
'[Eight days the fire bur]ns.' The seven-eight pair-formula.
'A fire burns in the palace(s).' tbʿr 'it burns' (G-yqtl 3fs of bʿr; cf. Hebrew bāʿar 'to burn' Exod 3:2).
'Flames in the temple.' nblʾut 'flame, ember' (cf. Hebrew lab[b]â).
'A day, a second, devours…' tʾikl 'it eats / consumes' (G-yqtl 3fs of ʾkl). The fire-as-eater.
'…the fire in the palace.'
'…flames in the temple.'
'A third, a fourth day…'
'…the fire devours in the palace.'
'…flames in the midst of the temple.'
'A fifth, a sixth day…'
'…the fire devours in the palace.'
'…flames in the midst of the temple.'

**THE FIRING CULMINATION**: 'And lo, on the seventh day…' mk 'and lo, behold' (presentative particle); the seven-day completion-formula. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. Gen 1's seven days; the seven-day liturgical-completion pattern.
'…the fire goes-out from the palace.' td 'it withdraws / dies down' (G-yqtl 3fs of dwd or ndd).
'The flame from the midst of the temple.'

'Silver was poured-out as bricks.' ṣb possibly 'cast, poured-out' (G-pass); lbnt 'bricks' (cf. Hebrew lĕbēnâ). The metallurgical-architectural completion: silver-bricks (= the precious sheathing of the palace-walls).
'Gold was molded as bricks.' nṣb 'standing-up, established' (cf. Hebrew niṣṣab). Gold-bricks alongside silver-bricks.
'Mighty Baʿlu rejoices.'
**BAʿLU'S TRIUMPHANT SHOUT**: 'My palace I have built of silver!' bht y 'my palace'; bnt 'I have built' (G-pf 1cs of bny); dt ksp 'of silver.' The triumph-of-construction.
'My temple of gold.' dtm 'of, with the' (relative-genitive); ḫrṣ 'gold.' The dual material-boast: silver palace, gold temple.
'Baʿlu prepares the appointments of his palace.' ʿdbt 'preparation, arrangement'; bht h 'his palace.'

'Hadd arranges [the arrangement of arrangements].' hd 'Hadad' = the Akkadian/Aramaic name of Baʿlu (the same storm-deity). Hadd-Hadad-Baʿlu correspondence; cf. the Aramean storm-god of 2 Sam 8:10 hădōrām.
**THE INAUGURATION FEAST**: '[He slaughters oxen, also shee]p.' The standard banquet-formula for the palace-dedication.
'[He fells bulls and] fatlings.'
'[Rams, calves] of a year.'
'[Lambs, abundance of kids].'
'[He cries (= invites) his brothers (= the gods) to his palace].'
'[His kin in the midst of his temple].'

**THE SEVENTY SONS — STRONG CROSS-CORPUS**: '[He cries the seventy sons of ʾAṯi]rat.' šbʿm bn ʾaṯrt 'seventy sons of ʾAṯirat' = the divine assembly. MANDATORY CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: cf. Deut 32:8 (LXX/4QDeutj 'sons of the gods/Israel') for the 70-nations / 70-sons motif; the divine council of seventy.
'…flowing-source.'
'…he calls.'

i18n.en: [KTU 1.4 col vii: the climactic column of the entire palace-building cycle. Baʿlu reverses himself on the window question — he now allows the window. With the window open, Baʿlu's voice (= thunder) goes forth from the palace and shakes the earth. This is the central theophany-passage of the Baal Cycle. MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE — the qlh qdš tr ʾarṣ line is THE Ugaritic-Hebrew Bible cognate-line for Psalm 29's qol-YHWH theophany.]

lines.notes: [Eighty, seventy cities/towns…]. pdr 'town' (cf. Hebrew bedēr — different etymology). Lost city-list-formula.
'Nine cities, ei[ghty]…'. Numerical-pair city-list (the towns under Baʿlu's dominion).
'Nine towns(?).' qrt 'town'; the numerical-iterative city-list.
'Baʿlu seized [...].'
'…his house / temple.'
'Baʿlu erects his palace.' trmm 'he erects' (D-yqtl 3ms of rwm; cf. Hebrew rām). The completion.
'He takes the throne of his kingship by force(?).' ʿrz 'strong, with might'; ksʾi mlkh 'his royal throne.'
'The dais of his dominion.' kḥṯ drkt 'dais of dominion' = the royal-establishment-formula.
'[And] Mighty Baʿlu answered.'
'I will offer / set in order (the feast), even I.' ʾaqry 'I will set in order, place' (G-yqtl 1cs of qry; cf. Hebrew qārâ Gen 24:12 'cause to occur').
'…(to) Kothar [-wa-]Khasis.'
'[Hear, O] Mightiest of warriors!' Vocative.
**THE WINDOW DEBATE RESUMED**: '[Sh]all I not place a window in the palac[e]?' bl 'shall I not?' — Baʿlu now ASKS the question Kothar had asked earlier.
'A skylight in the midst of the temple.'
**KOTHAR'S RESPONSE (preview)**: '[And Kothar]-wa-Khasis [answered].'
'…I shall reply, O Migh[t]y Baʿlu.'
'[I shall buil]d (it) of silver.'
'…of [gold I shall b]uild, of lapis-lazuli.'
'…they take.'

**BAʿLU CHANGES HIS MIND — MANDATORY MAJOR**: 'And Mighty Baʿlu answered.' The pivot — Baʿlu now accepts the window. Smith & Pitard 2009 vol 2 pp. 612ff: this reversal is the structural climax of the construction-arc.
'(No, no longer) — do not place the window [in the palace]…' Baʿlu's first response — STILL refusing(?). Reading uncertain — some editions take this as Baʿlu still hedging.
'…a skylight [in the midst of] the temple.'
'…Pidray [daughter of light].'
'…Ṭallay daughter of show[ers].'
**THE WINDOW-FEAR**: '[the Beloved of] ʾIlu, Yammu.' The reason for refusal: Yammu would come through the open window. Cf. Gen 7:11 (the cosmic-window-flood). STRONG CROSS-CORPUS.
'…they will deride.' (The princes mock his fearful refusal.)
**BAʿLU FINALLY ACCEPTS THE WINDOW**: '[And] Mighty Baʿlu answered.' Now the change-of-mind.
**BAʿLU OPENS THE WINDOW**: 'I shall place the window in the palace!' Baʿlu reverses himself — the window is opened.
'A skylight in the midst of the temple.'

**THE WINDOW IS OPENED**: 'He opens a window in the palace.' yptḥ 'he opens' (G-yqtl 3ms of ptḥ; cf. Hebrew pātaḥ); ḥln 'window' (= shorter form of ḥlln). The act of opening — the cosmic-window now allows Baʿlu's voice (thunder) to come forth.
'A skylight in the midst of the temple.'

**BAʿLU'S VOICE GOES FORTH — MANDATORY MAJOR**: 'He gives forth his voice in the clouds.' ytn 'he gives' (G-yqtl 3ms of ntn); qlh 'his voice'; b ʿrpt 'in the clouds.' STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. Ps 18:14 (=2 Sam 22:14) 'YHWH thundered from heaven, the Most High gave forth his voice'; Ps 29:3 qol-YHWH ʿal-hammāyim 'the voice of YHWH is on the waters'; Job 37:4-5. THE central theophany-line.

'…his lightning to the earth.' šr possibly 'release, send forth' (cf. Hebrew šārâ); brqm 'lightnings' (pl of brq; cf. Hebrew bĕrāqîm Ps 18:15). The lightning-as-storm-god-weapon. Cf. Ps 18:15 'he shot out his arrows and scattered them; lightnings flashing.'

**THE EARTH-SHAKING VOICE — MANDATORY MAJOR**: '(His) holy (voice) shakes the earth.' qdš 'holy' (cf. Hebrew qōdeš); tr 'shakes, makes-quiver' (G-yqtl 3ms of tww/twr 'to tremble'); ʾarṣ 'earth.' STRONG CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: cf. Ps 29:8 qol-YHWH yāḥîl midbār 'the voice of YHWH shakes the wilderness'; Hab 3:6 'he shook the earth'; Ps 68:9 'the earth trembled.' THE Ugaritic-Hebrew Bible theophany-parallel. This is the qlh qdš tr ʾarṣ line — note the reading qlh qdš in some editions reads as one phrase 'his holy voice.' MANDATORY MAJOR for Editor.

'(He) shatters the mountains be[neath]…'. rṯq 'shatters, splinters' (cf. Akk. rasāqu); ġrm 'mountains.' STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. Ps 29:5-6 'the voice of YHWH breaks the cedars'; Nah 1:5 'the mountains quake.'
'…the eternal mountains stagger.' tṭṭn 'they shake violently' (Gt-yqtl 3mp of nṭ); ġr ʿdm 'eternal mountains' (cf. Gen 49:26 'eternal hills' harĕrê ʿad). STRONG CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: Gen 49:26.
'The enemies of Baʿlu seize…'.

'…the haters of Hadd flee to the forests.' šnʾu 'haters' (cf. Hebrew śōnĕʾay Ps 18:18); yʿrm 'forests' (cf. Hebrew yaʿar). The theophany scatters the enemies. Cf. Ps 68:2 'as smoke is driven away, so drive them away.'
'…(his) hatreds(?) raise themselves.'
'…[li]ke slaves they pay tribute.' ʿbdm 'slaves, servants'; tšlmnn 'they make-peace, render-tribute' (D-yqtl 3mp + n-ending of šlm).
'Strong is your offspring, O Baʿlu.' ʿz 'strong'; šr 'offspring, root' (cf. Hebrew šōreš).
'…heights of Ṣapunu.'
'…beneath his face.'
'…the divin[e ones] are stirred up.' tʿrr 'they are roused' (Dt-yqtl 3mp); ʾilnym 'divinities.'
'…Baʿlu.'
'…(she) gives the head of gold(?).' Possibly the golden-head ornament for the palace.
'…she lifts her voice and cries.'
'…messengers.'
'…I have brought.'
**MÔT IS MENTIONED**: '…Môt.' mt 'Môt' (= Death personified) — the first mention of Death-as-deity. The transition to col viii's challenge.
'…(unto) Môt.'
'…king of eternity.' mlk ʿlmm 'eternal king' — Môt's epithet.
**MÔT-AS-SON-OF-GODS**: '…(to) Môt the son of the gods.' bn ʾilm mt 'Death the son of the gods' = Môt's full title. Cf. KTU 1.5 i 13.
'…Baʿlu.'
'…they are sent.'

i18n.en: [KTU 1.4 col viii: with the palace complete, Baʿlu now sends his messengers Gpn-wa-Ugar to Môt (Death personified) in the underworld. This proleptic challenge sets up the conflict that occupies Chapter 3 (KTU 1.5-1.6) of the Translation. The descent-to-the-underworld description is one of the few literary glimpses of Late-Bronze Northwest-Semitic underworld-cosmology.]

lines.notes: 'Then indeed (= now), set face!' The travel-formula opening — addressed to the messengers.
**THE COSMIC-MOUNTAIN-OF-THE-DEAD**: 'Toward Mount Trġziz…' trġzz a chthonic-mountain at the entrance to the underworld. Smith & Pitard 2009 vol 2 pp. 711-720.
'…toward Mount Ṯrmg.' ṯrmg the second chthonic mountain — the pair of underworld-mountains framing the descent.

'…toward the (two) hills (at) the throat of the earth.' tlm 'hills' (du); ġṣr 'throat, gorge' (cf. Hebrew ḥōq) — the throat-of-earth as entry-point to the underworld. Cf. Job 38:17 'gates of death'; Ps 9:14 'gates of death.'
'Lift the mountain upon (your) hands!' šʾu 'lift!' (G-impv); ġr 'mountain.' The mountain-lifting gesture — to enter the underworld one must lift the mountain-gate.
'(Lift the) Ḫalbu (= hill) upon the heights of the upper-hands.' ḫlb 'Ḫalbu / hill' (cf. Akk. ḫalbu); ẓr 'shoulder, peak'; rḥt 'palm, upper-hand.'

**DESCENT TO THE UNDERWORLD**: 'And descend (into) the house of the imprisoned!' rd 'descend!' (G-impv of yrd; cf. Hebrew yārad 'go down'); bt ḫpṯt 'house of the imprisoned-ones / pit-prison' (cf. Akk. ḫupšu). The descent-to-Sheol formula. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. Isa 14:15 'you shall be brought down to Sheol, to the recesses of the pit.'
'…(into) the earth, you are carried(?)…'
**MÔT THE SON OF THE GODS**: 'Toward Môt the son of the gods.' bn ʾilm mt 'Môt son of the gods' = Death's full title. The destination-deity is named.
'…unto the warrior of ʾIlu.' mhr 'warrior'; the underworld-warrior epithet.

lines.translit: ʾal . tqrb . l bn . ʾilm . mt
lines.notes: 'Do not draw near to Môt the son of the gods!' ʾal tqrb 'do not approach!' (G-yqtl-juss of qrb negative); the WARNING to the messengers — Môt is dangerous.

lines.translit: ʾal . yʿdbkm . k ʾimr . b ph
lines.notes: **MÔT-AS-DEVOURER — STRONG IMAGE**: 'Lest he set you like a lamb in his mouth!' ʾal yʿdbkm 'lest he put you' (G-yqtl-juss 3ms + 2mp suffix of ʿdb); k ʾimr 'like a lamb' (cf. Hebrew ʾimmar). Môt as the swallower of life — a signature underworld-image. Cf. Isa 5:14 'Sheol has opened wide its mouth.'
'…like a kid in the cleavage of his throat!' llʾi 'kid'; tbrn 'cleavage, breaking-point'; qn 'throat, neck' (cf. Hebrew qāneh). The devouring-image intensifies.
'The luminary of the gods, Šapšu.' nrt ʾilm 'lamp of the gods' = the sun-goddess Šapšu's standard epithet (cf. Hebrew nēr 'lamp' Ps 18:29). The sun-warning.
'…burns (with) the heat (of) heaven.' ṣḥrr 'glows, burns intensely' (G-yqtl 3fs of ṣḥrr); lṯʾu 'heat, weariness'; šmm 'heavens.' The intense-sun-as-warning-of-Môt's-realm.
'…(she is) in the hand of Môt the son of the gods.' Šapšu (the sun) crosses the underworld each night; she is the messenger BETWEEN realms.
'A thousand acres, broad as the sea.' rḥb 'broad' (cf. Hebrew rāḥāb); the vast-scale cosmic-geography.
'Ten thousand hectares…'.
**BAʿLU'S CHALLENGE TO MÔT — MANDATORY MAJOR**: '…Message of Mighty Baʿlu.' THE proleptic challenge that drives the entire next chapter (KTU 1.5-1.6 = Chapter 3 of the WoH Translation).
'[Word of the Mightiest] of warriors.'
'…my palace I have built…'.
'…of silver, the temple [of gold].'
'…contemn the gods(?).'
'…his brothers.'
'[I called the seventy sons of ʾAṯirat].' (Cf. 1.4 vi 58.)
'…Môt (the) (only/one).'
'…confines him(?).'
'…draws near.'
'…confines.'
'…Baʿlu.'
'…they depart.'
'…unto Môt the son of the gods.' The messengers reach the destination — the cliff-hanger ending of KTU 1.4 / Chapter 2. Chapter 3 picks up with Môt's reply in KTU 1.5 i.
'…they are sent.'
'…Baʿlu (and) Môt.'
'…Môt is strong.' Foreshadowing Môt's-victory in KTU 1.5 vi.
